note: The content_hash vectors are FROZEN, and they do not come from the C# in src/. They were produced by a reference implementation of Translation::computeHash — the website's — and that implementation was itself checked against reality first: run over a real 690-line published translation sitting on disk, it reproduced the file_hash the server had issued for that file. So these are not 'what our code does', they are what the server does. A hash that only agrees with itself would pass every check and make every translation in existence look permanently out of sync. The `v2-*` vectors (the fields of the format 2, written after v and t) come from a SECOND reference written in Python from the specification alone (json.dumps, separators (',',':'), ensure_ascii=False, keys sorted by UTF-8 bytes) — not from the C# and not yet from the website, whose Translation::computeHash must reproduce them: until it does, a format 2 file is not publishable.

cases.why: an empty translation still hashes — the uuid is content too
the tag is part of the content, not a decoration

keys sort by byte, not by culture — ORDINAL puts 'A' before '_uuid' before 'a'; a culture-aware sort puts 'a' first and produces a different document on one machine and not another — and the uuid sorts among them
accents stay as themselves — literal, not escaped: both are valid JSON, only one is the right bytes (JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE, and the mod agrees)
and so does anything else — the games that most need translating are these ones
a solidus is not escaped — PHP escapes it unless told not to; we tell it not to
quotes are escaped, in keys as well as in values
and so are backslashes — a game full of \n literals would break otherwise
a tab uses its short form, not \u0009
a newline too — game text is full of them
and the rest go to lower-case \u00xx — four digits, whatever the character
metadata keys are excluded — a counter must not change a file's identity

cases.why: a line whose text begins with an underscore is content: it changes the file's identity like any other line
the order they arrive in is irrelevant — two machines meet lines in different orders
the reference order of the case above
an absent tag stays absent: it is NOT filled in with the default — the file is hashed AS WRITTEN, and tidying anything produces a different hash for a file nobody edited
a null value stays null, not an empty string; they are different documents
a pre-tag entry stays a bare string — an old published file must still match
and the two forms coexist in one file, which is what an old file looks like

U+2028 and U+2029, in a value AND in a key, are written as themselves, like every character above 0x1F. PHP's json_encode writes them as \u2028 / \u2029 unless JSON_UNESCAPED_LINE_TERMINATORS is passed: a published file that holds one has a different hash on the site than in every mod already in players' hands, and the mods are the reference
U+007F, < > & and the apostrophe are plain characters: written as themselves. PHP escapes the four HTML ones only under JSON_HEX_TAG, JSON_HEX_AMP, JSON_HEX_APOS — flags that must stay off
backspace, form feed and carriage return use their short forms, and every other control character below 0x20 goes to lower-case \u00xx (U+001F, U+0001)
a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is written as itself, not as a surrogate pair of \u escapes
a term mark is part of the content: it is written after v and t, only when true
form ids sort by BYTE (f1, f10, f2), not by the number inside: the order every language gives to text
what a template takes from an entry: one form, or one per class; template ids and class names sort by byte at both levels
the class an entry gives in each template it governs, template ids in byte order
a template line carries how it was made
links stay an array in the line's own order, each member in the order to, form, case, by, was and only the ones held; quote, backslash, slash and accents are written as the format 1 writes them
the position of a link is the N of its marker: the same two links in the other order are another document
the keys a person refused are a set: written sorted by byte, so two writers listing the same ones agree
every field in one file, beside a plain line and a pre-tag one: the fields are written after v and t of their own line only
a field that is there and empty is NOT written: this file hashes as the plain line of sync/content_hash/one-line-one-tag
identical content is in sync, whatever the change counter says — asked FIRST: without it, a file edited back to what the server holds would be offered for upload forever
my changes on an unmoved server is an upload — nothing of theirs is at risk
their changes on an untouched file is a download — nothing of mine is at risk
both moved is a merge, and only the mod can settle it line by line
no ancestor plus local work is a conflict, not a download — that is a translation somebody built themselves and never published, and this case decides whether their work survives
no ancestor and nothing of mine is still a download — there is nothing to lose
nothing published means nothing to reconcile — not an upload nobody asked for
the settings are in no content hash: identical lines with a font or a rule changed here is something to upload — the Manager said 'Up to date' beside the mod's 'settings changed — not uploaded yet'
settings that did not move add nothing
a setting changed here while the site moved is a merge — downloading over it would lose the setting
with the settings untouched it is Decide's own answer
the four words every piece of software has used for thirty years: this read 'In step' until somebody pointed out that nobody outside a version-control habit says it
'Behind' said the same thing to nobody
'Ahead' said the same thing to nobody
'Diverged' is the version-control word; 'Conflict' is the one every program uses
